data: Status: planned (wave 2). No code exists. The package name is provisional.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Area Criterion reading exact equality of the values read against the oracle round trip Go writes and astropy reads, and the other way round, with identical arrays hostile input go test -fuzz for panics; a limit on the allocation a hostile header can ask for Oracles: astropy.io.fits (BSD-3-Clause) and fitsverify. Corpus: NASA’s FITS sample files and astropy’s test data. Every item also needs unit tests at 100% coverage and a performance table against the reference.
data.references#References: Subject Reference the format IAU FITS Working Group, FITS Standard 4.0, 2018
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid:
FITS 4.0: 2880-byte blocks of 80-character cards, big-endian data, images, binary tables, and compressed images (Rice, GZIP and HCOMPRESS).
Whether to fork or to audit an existing package is open. astrogo/fitsio (BSD-3-Clause) is archived on GitHub, and a fork would keep its notice.

data: Status: planned (wave 2, the first item of go-sciio). No code exists. The package name is provisional (go-hdf5 belongs to a third party and is not available).
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Area Criterion reading exact equality of integers, strings and raw floats against the reference reader round trip Go writes and h5py reads, and the arrays are identical; Go reads files that h5py wrote hostile input go test -fuzz for panics; a limit on the allocation a hostile header can ask for Oracles: h5py, h5dump and h5ls from the HDF Group, whose C library is the reference reader. Corpus: the HDF Group’s example files and h5py’s test files. Every item also needs unit tests at 100% coverage and a performance table against the reference.
data.references#References: Subject Reference the format HDF Group, HDF5 File Format Specification, version 3.0
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid:
An HDF5 reader and writer: superblock versions 0 to 3, object headers v1 and v2, B-trees v1 and v2, the fractal heap, the local heap, chunked layout, the deflate, shuffle and fletcher32 filters, and the global heap for variable-length data. mat (v7.3) and netcdf (NetCDF-4) are built on it and inherit its bugs.
Whether to audit and wrap an existing pure-Go package (scigolib/hdf5, MIT, young, partial write support) or to write the package here is undecided; it couples the whole organisation to one choice. Any audit includes hostile-input limits: allocation caps and recursion depth.

data: Status: planned (wave 2). No code exists. The package name is provisional.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Area Criterion reading exact equality of the values read against the oracle round trip Go writes and SciPy (v4 to v7) or h5py (v7.3) reads, with identical arrays; Go reads their files hostile input go test -fuzz for panics; a limit on the allocation a hostile header can ask for scipy.io (loadmat, savemat) is the oracle for v4, v5 and v7, and does not support v7.3. Corpus: SciPy’s scipy/io/matlab/tests/data (BSD-3-Clause). Every item also needs unit tests at 100% coverage and a performance table against the reference.
data.references#References: Subject Reference v4, v5, v7, v7.3 MathWorks, MAT-File Format
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: MAT v4: a 20-byte header per matrix. MAT v5 and v7: a 128-byte header and tagged data elements, with zlib compression (miCOMPRESSED) in v7. MAT v7.3: an HDF5 file with a 512-byte user block, the MATLAB_class attribute, complex numbers as compound types and sparse matrices as groups, written and read on top of h5.

data.references#References: Subject Reference the formats Unidata, NetCDF File Format Specification conventions the CF conventions
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: NetCDF classic in its three variants (CDF-1, CDF-2 with 64-bit offsets and CDF-5): big-endian, with a record dimension. NetCDF-4: HDF5 with dimension scales, the “classic model” subset, on top of h5. The CF conventions’ units attribute, which is in the UDUNITS syntax; the planned units package of go-units parses it.
